goal: Limit concurrent client connections and reserve file descriptors for IPC listeners.
Support per-listener max-connections configuration via -ipcbind options.
reviewability: Ready to merge. Reviewers have thoroughly tested and approved the latest iteration.

categories.name: ipc
why: P2 because it fixes a gap in file descriptor accounting and prevents IPC connections from starving core resources or crashing the node.
Establishes an extensible socket option parsing format on -ipcbind for future IPC capabilities.

result.summary: This pull request adds connection limits and file descriptor reservations for IPC listeners configured via `-ipcbind`. It introduces an inline option format (`-ipcbind=unix:<path>,max-connections=<n>`), defaulting each listener to 16 connection slots up to a maximum cap of 256, and integrates these reservations into startup file descriptor checks.
result.problem: Previously, IPC listeners accepted unlimited connections without accounting for file descriptors during startup, allowing runaway connection counts to exhaust descriptors, starve P2P/RPC sockets, or trigger startup abort assertions.

resolved_concerns: Avoided Windows path ambiguity with colons by switching the option delimiter to commas and adding URL decoding (ryanofsky).
Prevented integer overflow in initialization FD calculations and capped aggregate IPC reservations at 256 (xyzconstant, ViniciusCestarii).
Retained full resolved socket path in logs and startup error messages (ViniciusCestarii).
Separated the libmultiprocess subtree update into a dedicated merged PR (#35684) prior to final integration here (Sjors, enirox001).

result.card: This pull request allows `-ipcbind` listeners to limit maximum simultaneous client connections using an inline `,max-connections=<n>` socket option syntax. It reserves file descriptors for IPC listeners during node startup, capping per-socket limits at 256 to prevent resource exhaustion and arithmetic overflows. The PR has strong consensus and code/tested approvals from multiple contributors and maintainers, with no open blockers.
